prompt: Below is `verifyWebhook`, the verification function on a webhook RECEIVER endpoint. For every inbound request it first recomputes an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body and compares it against the `X-Signature` header using a constant-time compare, and only afterward checks whether the `X-Timestamp` header falls within the `MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` freshness window. The logic is correct — valid, fresh requests are accepted and forged or stale ones are rejected — but the endpoint is currently under a replay flood of huge volumes of stale, out-of-window requests, and CPU usage is spiking. Walk through why CPU is being burned on traffic that was always going to be rejected, then optimize the verification path so it does less work per request without changing what gets accepted, what gets rejected, or the constant-time property of the real signature comparisons.
